messages:
alex: heads up — ran the 'kepler' split-bench this morning: comparing kepler-fused, flash-v2, and paged-attn across H100 / A100 / L40S. uploads + raw CSVs in s3://redwood-perf/kepler-split/1744506780/ :thumbsup:
marta: nice. quick take? any regressions vs last week's sweep?
devon: quick summary (H100, seq sweep, batch sweep):
- seq=512 bsz=16: flash-v2 p50 8ms, kepler p50 9.5ms, paged p50 11.2ms
- seq=2048 bsz=4: flash-v2 p50 18ms, kepler p50 22ms, paged p50 25ms
- seq=4096 bsz=2: flash-v2 throughput 11.4k tok/s, kepler 9.1k, paged 8.0k; p95: flash-v2 260ms, kepler 310ms, paged 420ms
- mem: kepler 42GB @ seq4096, paged 36GB but has 1-2 sudden 60GB spikes when KV eviction kicks in
anya: observed something funky: p95 oscillation lines up with KV cache hit ratio dropping below ~0.85. logs: 
```
2024-10-10 09:14:23.321 KVCache: hit_ratio=0.82 evicting 128MB
2024-10-10 09:14:23.622 KernelSelector: chose=paged-attn reason="mem_limit"
```
alex: yep saw the same. kernel selector fallback path picks paged for a short tail which kills latency. looks like cost-model misestimates streaming prefix reuse.
marta: where are the perf profiles? can we get a flamegraph for the spike window?
devon: uploaded flamegraphs and perf.data to s3 + gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kepler-split-1744506780. flame shows heavy memcpy + compute imbalance during paged spill. also attached kernel timelines.
ci-bot: build #2319 for perf/kepler-split completed — artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/perf/2319/
infra-bot: test cluster h100-qa-4 scheduled teardown in 30m — extend? @alex
alex: extend 2h please, re-running L40S batch matrix after fixing prefetch flag.
anya: small repro command if you want to re-run locally: 
```
./bench/run.sh --model llama-13b --seq 4096 --batch 2 --kernels "kepler,flash-v2,paged" --device h100 --prefetch on --kv-evict-threshold 0.9 --profile flame --out s3://redwood-perf/kepler-split/1744506780/
```
marta: can you also try: --prefetch off and --continuous-batching on (we suspect prefetch+kv-evict interaction).
devon: scheduled that run now on A100 and L40S, will post delta. initial A100 numbers look similar but kepler gap to flash-v2 shrinks at seq<=1024. L40S shows flash-v2 not always faster due to different memcpy kernels.
anya: found small selector bug: when estimated memory delta within 200MB, we accidentally bias towards page-compat kernels. open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kepler-runtime/pull/478 — fixes comparator and adds unit for kv-hit thresholds.
alex: great. action items: (1) devon re-run with prefetch off+cont-batching, (2) marta add cost-model logging to selector for next sweep, (3) anya & devon investigate mem spike path. anyone want to add?
marta: will add selector logging; also add a metric that tracks "kernel_switch_count" per request so we can correlate.
devon: I'll post new CSVs ~in 45m. FYI I also tried a micro-variant of flash-v2 (flash-v2a) which trades a copy for less branching — interestingly it reduces p95 by ~12% at seq2048 bsz4 on H100.
anya: sounds promising. if flash-v2a is stable, we should add it to kernel-candidate list for Dedicated pools.
alex: agreed. once we have second sweep results, we should do a quick canary rollout to a low-traffic pool and monitor kernel_switch_count + kv_hit_ratio alarms.
ci-bot: perf-comparison diff: https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/diff/kepler-split/2319 — shows p95 regressions on paged for long seq on H100.
infra-bot: teardown extended to +2h.
devon: uploaded second run with --prefetch off + continuous batching on H100/A100/L40S. short notes: paged p95 improved when prefetch disabled but throughput dropped ~8%. kepler unaffected. flash-v2a keeps lead on p95. CSVs: s3://redwood-perf/kepler-split/1744506780/run2/
marta: perfect. I'll compile a short doc for product showing latency/throughput tradeoffs per kernel and recommended defaults per workload.
alex: thanks all. we'll follow up in next runtime sync if any surprises. :rocket:
